cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7), and he's just said that where sin increased, grace increased all the more (Romans 5:20). So he asks it straight out, no tiptoeing: "Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?"

cards.question: True or false: Paul says believers should keep on sinning so that grace can increase.
Paul gives a hard no to sinning so grace can increase. What reason does he give for why believers can't keep living in sin?

cards.text: Then Paul brings up baptism: everyone baptized into Christ Jesus was baptized into His death. So, he says, we were buried with Him through baptism into death.

cards.question: Believers were buried with Christ through baptism into death. Just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, what may they do?
True or false: Paul says believers who have been united with Christ in His death will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

cards.text: Then Paul says our old self was crucified with Him.
That happened so the body of sin might be rendered powerless. Powerless, like the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with, still swearing they had a little charge left.

cards.question: The old self was crucified with Christ. According to Paul, what should believers no longer be?

cards.text: Anyone who has died has been freed from sin, and if we died with Christ, Paul says we believe we will also live with Him. Sin can knock all it wants, friend, but the old you is NOT answering that door.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that since Christ was raised from the dead, He can still die again.
Paul says death no longer has dominion over Christ. When Christ died to sin, how many times did He die?

cards.text: But the life He lives, He lives to God. So Paul says you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
Paul says, "Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires." Sin doesn't get the throne, friend, and it doesn't even get a parking spot.

cards.question: Paul says not to present the parts of the body to sin as instruments of wickedness. Instead, present yourselves to God as those brought from death to life, and present the parts of the body to Him as instruments of ___.

cards.text: Then Paul makes a promise: sin shall not be your master. And friend, he tells them exactly why.

cards.question: Paul says sin shall not be their master, because they are not under law, but under ___.
